and more than a third of the people perished.
And likewise it happened also in Syria, and in Egypt, and especially in Persia.
In the city of Bukhara, eighteen thousand biers of the dead were carried out in a single day.
And those who died were:
in a short time,
a span of three months,
one million, six hundred and fifty thousand people.
And in Samarkand,
within two months, two hundred and thirty-six thousand died.
It is said
that from the beginning of the world there had not been a pestilence like this.
And in the year 1369 [of the Greeks = 1057/1058 AD],
the Ghuzz were defeated,
and one thousand two hundred men of them were killed;
and Qutalmish, their leader, fled with those who escaped with him to the mountain of Sinjar.
And the people of Sinjar shut the gates of the city against them,
and mocked them.
Now when the Sultan heard what had happened,
he grew resolute in his spirit,
and wanted to go to Mosul.
The Caliph, however, was not willing,
and he sent to him and said to him:
"It is not right for you to go now,
but wait until your forces gather and come from Persia."
He, however, became even more enraged and said:
"Now I know that your intention toward us is not sincere.
At first you counselled me
that you yourself should not go,
but send forces.
And I accepted it from you,
and lo, my forces have perished;
and now again you counsel me the very same thing!"
Up to this time the Sultan had been thirteen months in Baghdad,
and he went out and had not yet seen the Caliph.
And he commanded,
and they pitched his pavilion outside.
And his forces that were ready assembled,
and they ravaged the districts of the eastern side of Baghdad,
and they took their bridges because of the boats.
And he went and encamped against Tikrit,
and demanded aid from them.
They, however, said:
"We belong to the Ma'addites,
and without the command of al-Basasiri, their leader,
we are not able to give anything."
And the Sultan was incensed,
and put them to the sword,
and took captive from them many women and children.
And when they submitted to him,
he made peace with them.
And he went to Beth Waziq,
and its inhabitants gave him aid.
And from there he went to Mosul,
and found al-Basasiri
